lines.text: Yeah. I like sleeping in late. So sometimes, I wake up at 11:00. On those days, if I know I won't wake up until 11:00, I'll take a shower the night before, before I go to bed. How about you, Sarah? When do you usually wake up ?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Well, I like everyday to be the same. So I wake up everyday at 8 o'clock.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: 8:00. And I always do the same thing. First, I make coffee right away. Then I wake up my kids and we have breakfast together at about 8:30.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes. We usually have something easy like bread and yogurt and fruit.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: I like to have coffee every morning whether I wake up at 6:00 or at 10:00. I'm still going to have coffee. But I often skip breakfast. Do you always eat breakfast everyday?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes. If I don't eat breakfast, I'm so hungry. What about lunch? What time do you have lunch?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Lunch is the same everyday for me. I always eat lunch at 12:30 PM. So whenever I wake up, I do some things and then I always have lunch at 12:30 PM, just half past noon. And I always have a simple lunch. Maybe some soup or spaghetti or a sandwich. Something light, and it's always at half past noon. What time do you eat lunch?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: That's interesting. I have breakfast at the same time everyday but lunch is always at a different time.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Because I'm busy in the morning. I go out, maybe I go shopping. Sometimes, I clean the house. So I might have lunch at 11 o'clock or 12 o'clock. Sometimes as late as 2:30.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Oh, that's getting late.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes. But it's always easy lunch like you. Maybe crackers and cheese or a sandwich or a baked potato.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: So Sarah, what can you tell me about your hometown?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: My hometown. Well, my hometown is called Eau Claire, Wisconsin. And it's a really great city.
There are about 80,000 people. There are lots of things to do. There are three movie theatres. I love to watch movies.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Me too.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: There's lots of shopping. You can find anything you want there. There are a lot of malls and stores.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Are there many restaurants?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes. The thing I like is you can eat any type of food. There are Chinese restaurants and Korean restaurants, Italian restaurants. There is a big variety of restaurants, and they're all good.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: That sounds great. What about parks? Are there many places to see nature in your town?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes. We have a lot of rivers, and lakes and hills. My hometown has four seasons. So in summer, it's great because there are lots of lakes to swim in, lots of forests to play in. In winter, there is a lot of snow. So you can go ice skating or ice fishing or even skiing.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Wow. That sounds really fun.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yeah. It's a really nice city. It's also really safe. There are lots of nice people there.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Good. Is there much to do at night?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Well, maybe, maybe not. There's not many things to do at night. There aren't any nightclubs. There aren't many bars. So actually, maybe there isn't much night life.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: That's okay. It sounds like a nice place to have a family.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yeah. It is. It's a great place to have a family. There's lots of good schools and libraries.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So John, where are you from?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: My hometown is very small. It's a little town in the countryside, in Wisconsin. There are only 5,000 people there.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Wow. There aren't very many people.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: No, it's very small. There aren't very many businesses. There isn't a shopping mall. There are a lot of grocery stores. And there are a lot of gas stations. But there isn't much to do there.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Oh really? Are there any movie theaters?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, there is one movie theater. So that's a nice thing to do. In fact, there are many screens in the theater. There are eight different movies showing.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: How about at night? What's fun to do – how about at night? Is there very much night life?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Yeah, there is not so much. But there is a bowling alley. It's fun to go bowling with friends. There's a bowling alley and the movie theater. There is one restaurant where you can go for tacos and burritos. And there's one more restaurant for pizza and spaghetti.

But during the daytime, you can go to the park. There's a river that goes through the town. So in the middle of town, there's a river. And there's a park that goes along both sides of the river. And at the park, there is a tennis court and a disc golf course.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Disc golf?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Yeah. I like to play disc golf with my friends. It's really fun. And after we finish playing disc golf, we usually go to the pizza restaurant.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Oh, I see. How about schools? Are there very many schools?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Let's see. No, there aren't very many. There is only one elementary school, one junior high school and one high school. That's it.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Interesting.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Yeah. There aren't very many schools but the town doesn't need more schools because there aren't very many people there.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I see. Are there any mountains?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: No. The whole area is very flat. There are no mountains but there are a lot of trees. In fact, there are trees on my town's sign because my town is famous for all the trees on every street.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Oh wow. It sounds like a great city.

lines.text: Hey Meg, so let's talk about our life history.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Okay, let's do it.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So first, when were you born?

lines.text: Oh!

lines.text: Okay, so when did you graduate high school?

lines.text: Oh my gosh. Really!

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What about you ?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, I graduated high school in 1987.

lines.text: Ah, when I was three years old.

lines.text: And when did you graduate from college?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, I took more time than normal.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And when did you get your first job?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I got my first job when I was 17 years old, I think. When I was still in high school.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What did you do?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I worked at a wedding shop, a wedding dress shop, so I helped to assist the customers and clean the dresses.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's a cool job.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ah, it wasn't so great actually.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Because brides can get a little crazy.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I can imagine.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What about you? When was your first job?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, my first unofficial job was when I was 13. I was a dishwasher.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, at a restaurant?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, and I think it was illegal because I was 13. But yeah, I was a dishwasher. But then my first official job was at McDonald's.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, what did you do there?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I made the filet-o-fish. But I got fired.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, why?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Also, again I lied about my age. So actually wait, I was 14, and I lied and said I was 15 and they fired me, but I worked there for three months.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, and you got paid?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And I got paid.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, that's good at least.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It was good times. Good times.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: (Laughter)

lines.text: OK, so when did you meet your best friend?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I met my best friend in 2007, so about 10 years ago. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh gosh, I met my best friend in high school, so I was a sophomore, a second year student, so that was 1984 or 1985.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow! So you've been best friends for a long time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: A long time, yeah, yep. So how about phones? When did you get your first phone?

lines.text: Hmm! I think I got my first phone when I was also 17, the same year I had my first job. It was my first cell-phone, was that year. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, I got my first phone also when I was 17, but it was a real phone. My parents gave me my own phone line in my house, so I had a phone in my room. Back then that was common in the 80s, so young high school people would have their own phone in their house.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, some of my friends had that when I was growing up also, but I wasn't lucky enough to get my own phone until I could pay for it myself.

lines.text: Abidemi, what did you do for summer break?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: For summer break, I went to visit some countries in Asia.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, what countries?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I visited Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, and Myanmar.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, great. What did you do in each country?

lines.speaker: Abidemi

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What foods did you eat?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I don’t remember the names but I just remembered that they were all good.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Thai food is so good.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Did you go anymore in Thailand like the beach or the forest?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I was more interested in nature, so I traveled from Bangkok to Chiang Mai and Chang Rai, and I went trekking and rode elephants. So that was one of the highlights of my trip.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh nice. How long was the trek?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: The trek was about a day. It was a trek for 2, 3 hours but then we also stayed overnight in a community in the hills. And then the next day, we trekked for a little bit to come back to the city.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. So was Thailand the first stop?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes. It was my first stop. It was supposed to be the shortest stop but I loved it so much that I spent more time there.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: After Thailand, where did you go?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: From Thailand, I moved on by land to Laos.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And what did you do in Laos?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: In Laos, I mainly was in the northern part of the country, and I went zip-lining .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh fun!

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: It was fun. So—

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So zip-lining is going flying from tree to tree ?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: That’s correct. So that was about two days’ worth of zip-lining, and we stayed overnight in a big tree house.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, how fun.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: It was quite an experience .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I really enjoyed it.

lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: Aimee

lessons.title: Is your house cold in the winter?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. My question today, is your house cold in winter?

Yes. My house is very cold in winter, but my heater is warm and my jacket is warm, and my sweater is warm, and my hood is warm. But my house is not warm. My house is very cold outside. It is very cold in winter, but in summer it is not cold. In summer, it is very hot.
So my question for you is, is your house cold in winter?
Hi, my name is Sarah and I will say 10 things about myself using articles "a" and "the" and I'll talk about what is in my house.

Okay. I have a washing machine. I also have a fridge. I have a small stove. I want a bigger stove. I don't have an electric toaster. I do have a vacuum cleaner, and I have a TV. I have an air conditioner, and I have a microwave. I want another TV.
So how about you? Can you say 10 things using articles about things in your house? You should try.

lessons.title: Where do you go in the morning?

lines.text: Hi, my name is Neri and I am from Belize. My question is, where do you go in the morning?

In the morning I go to the gym. I exercise and I walk on the treadmill. I lift some weights and I get sweaty. I like going to the gym. I walk to the gym because it is very close. It doesn't take long, and it's an exercise or a warmup. Before I exercise. I like going to the gym in the morning.
My question to you is, where do you go in the morning?
Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. My question is, where are your friends from?
My friends are from America. My friends are from Argentina. My friends are from Venezuela, and my friends are from Spain. I don't have friends from France.
And you, where are your friends from?

lessons.title: Is your house or apartment new?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Dandara. I'm from Brazil. And my question is, is your house or apartment new?

My apartment is not new. It is old, but comfortable. I like living here. My apartment is in a busy area. It is close to restaurants and shops. The furniture in my apartment is very simple and it has some decorations. My apartment is perfect for me.
And what about you?
Is your house or apartment new?
Hello, my name is Kyle. I am from the UK. My question for you today is do you play sports?
I play many sports. My favorite sports to play are that's football, basketball, and many others. But I don't like to play baseball. Do you play sports?
Hello, my name is Nerry and I am from Belize. My question today is, do you have any pets?

Yes, I have one pet. My pet is a dog and my pet's name is Gray. Gray is a brown dog. Gray loves to eat and he loves to bark. Gray is outside sleeping right now because his belly is full. Gray, eats a lot of food, and he also barks a lot. Sometimes Gray sits right here beside me and he looks at me when Gray is feeling happy. He wags his tail when he is feeling sad. He lays down like this. Gray is a part of my family and I love my pet. Gray. Gray is my best friend. Gray is my pet dog.
My question for you today is do you have any pets?
Hello, my name is Julie. I'm from America. The question is, what foods do you dislike?
Well, I love sushi, and I love tacos, and I love pizza, but I dislike onions. I also dislike olives, and I hate tomatoes. I also hate cucumbers.
What about you? What foods do you dislike?

lessons.title: Where do you go on the weekend?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Susan. I am from Armenia. My question is, where do you go on the weekend?

I go to the beach every weekend. I don't stay at home. I always go there with my friend. We spend a lot of time there. We relax. I enjoy the view. I read a book. I do my lessons. Usually I paint. My friend doesn't paint with me. She doesn't like it. She listens to music. She is always on her phone. She doesn't work there. She just enjoys her time.
And you, where do you go on the weekend?

lessons.title: Who do you eat dinner with?

lines.text: Hi, my name is Billie, and I am from South Africa. Today, I will talk about who do I it dinner with? Who do I eat dinner with?

I eat dinner with my family. I eat dinner with my mom, my dad, my sister, my other sister, and my younger brother. We are six. I am the number six. So I eat dinner with five people, my family. Thank you.
Hello, my name is Maggie. I am from America, and my question is, what is your house like?

Well, first I live in an apartment. I live on the first floor of my apartment. There is an elevator, but I don't need it. My apartment has two bedrooms and two bathrooms. There is also a kitchen and a large living room. My favorite room in my house is the patio. This is outside. I enjoy sitting and drinking coffee outside on the patio.
What is your house like?

lessons.title: Is your apartment big or small?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, is your apartment big?

My apartment is not big. My apartment has one bedroom. The bedroom is very big. It has a bed and a desk. The window is big. The living room is small. It has a sofa and a TV. My kitchen is small, but the window is big. The bathroom is not big, but it has a bathtub.
How is your apartment?

lessons.title: Is your house near the station?

lines.text: Hi, my name is Nerry, and I am from Belize. My question today is, do you live near a train station?

No. I do not live near a train station. In Belize, we do not have trains. What we have is buses, motorcycles, cars, and planes. I'm excited to ride a train for the first time. My question to you is, do you live near a train station?
Hi, my name is Billy and I live in South Africa. Today I will talk about what is on my schedule today.

What is on my schedule today? Today is big holiday, so I don't go to work. I want to clean my house, and I want to cook a very good meal or food for dinner. My schedule is not busy today, so I am happy. Bye.

lessons.title: Is your house cold in winter?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. My question today, is your house cold in winter?

Yes. My house is very cold in winter, but my heater is warm and my jacket is warm, and my sweater is warm, and my hood is warm. But my house is not warm. My house is very cold outside. It is very cold in winter, but in summer it is not cold. In summer, it is very hot.
So my question for you is, is your house cold in winter?

lessons.title: Do you want a new pet?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, do you want a new pet?

Yes, I want a pet. I don't have a pet now. I want a cat. They are cute and furry. I also want a parrot. They are very cute and colorful. They can talk and sing. I don't want a lizard. They eat insects.
Do you want a new pet?
Hello, my name is Dandara. I'm from Brazil, and my question is, where are you from?

I'm from Sao Paulo. Sao Paulo is a big city. There are many people here. People often travel to Sao Paulo to find a new job. I live with my friends here. My family lives in another city. I love Sao Paulo because there are many things to do here. For example, you can go shopping, visit museums, and go to different restaurants.
What about you? Where are you from?
Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from America, and my question is, who visits you on the holidays?

My sister visits me on the holidays. She is my younger sister. She sleeps at my house. She eats at restaurants with me. She does not like meat. She eats vegetables. She likes to dance. She dances with me at parties. She visits with my friends. She drives to see my brother here. He has a wife and a baby. She likes to hold the baby. My sister has fun when she visits me on the holidays.
My question for you is who visits you on the holidays?

lessons.title: What does your favorite shop sell?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I'm from America, and my question is, what does your favorite shop sell ?

My favorite shop is a coffee shop . It sells coffee and tea. It also sells t-shirts and coffee mugs . The shop also serves really nice coffee. It also serves really nice tea with honey . The shop has chairs and tables outside. It has nice big chairs upstairs . It has many plants inside. The shop is near my house. I like to buy tea and work on my computer there. The shop does not sell books like another coffee shop in town.
My question for you is, what does your favorite shop sell?
Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, how are you today?
I'm very good. Today is a nice day. It is cold, but it is sunny. I feel energetic. I had breakfast. I'm not tired. I'm not sleepy. I am at home. I am with my family.
How are you today?
Hello, my name is Dandara. I'm from Brazil, and my question is, what shop sells cheap clothes?
There is a shop near my house. It's called Forever 21. This shop has good prices. It sells jackets, t-shirts and pants. Jackets cost about $30. Pants cost about $15, and t-shirts cost about $10.

I like to go there. My mom also loves going there. She likes to buy t-shirts because she thinks t-shirts are very cheap there. My brother does not like to go there. He doesn't like shopping. My sister and I often go there together. We like to buy jackets there.
What about you? What shops sell cheap clothes where you live?

lessons.title: Who spends a lot of time with you?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Syuzan. I am from Armenia. My question is, who spends a lot of time with you?

My friend spends a lot of time with me. Her name is Lisa. We live abroad together. We study at the same university. She studies very hard. She doesn't miss any lessons. She helps me a lot. Lisa always plans our day. After university, we don't go home. We go for a walk. She takes pictures of our city. She enjoys sunsets every day. Lizanne doesn't like loneliness. She's always with me. I am happy about that.
Tell me who spends a lot of time with you.

lessons.title: What kind of pies do you like?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. My question is, what pies do you like?
I like pies. I love pies. I like apple pie. I like cherry pie and I love key lime pie, but I do not like lemon pie, and I do not like banana pie.
What pies do you like?
Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, who goes to school?

My nephew goes to school. His name is Mickey. He's 13 years old. He goes to junior high school. The school is near a lake. Mickey loves to play the piano. He plays the piano in class. He's very good at the piano. He has many prizes. Mickey has a younger sister. He doesn't have a brother. His sister goes to school, too.
Do you go to school?

lessons.title: What do you do on your lunch break?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Kyle. I am from the UK. My question for you today is what do you do on your lunch break?
What do you do on your lunch break? I go on my phone, I eat my lunch. I rest.
What do you do on your lunch break?
Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, where is your family from?

My mom is from Osaka. Osaka is in Japan. It is in the west of Japan. It is a big city. My dad is from Yokohama. Yokohama is also in Japan. It is near Tokyo. Tokyo is the capital of Japan. My husband is not from Japan. He is from Romania. I live with my husband in Bucharest. Bucharest is the capital of Romania. I don't live in Japan.
Where is your family from?

lessons.title: Does your town have nice parks?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Lyra. I am from Kosovo. My question is, does your town have nice parks?

Yes, it does. My town has three beautiful parks. Two of the parks are small. One park is a big, the big park is my favorite one. It has tall green trees. It doesn't have colorful flowers. I love to visit this park. Children love to play in this park. Grownups love to exercise and run in this park. My favorite thing is to take walks in the park. This park is wonderful. I hope a lot of people get to visit it.
Now you tell me, does your town have nice parks?

lessons.title: What do you do on the weekend?

lines.text: Hi, my name is Billy and I live in South Africa. Today, I will talk about what do I do on the weekend? What do I do on the weekend?

On the weekend, I go shopping. I buy food. I buy snacks. I buy many things for the house. On the weekend, I also sometimes clean. I clean the house, and sometimes I sleep or watch a movie with my friends or family.
Thank you.
Hello, my name is Julie. I'm from America. The question is, what foods do you dislike?
Well, I love sushi, and I love tacos, and I love pizza, but I dislike onions. I also dislike olives, and I hate tomatoes. I also hate cucumbers.
What about you? What foods do you dislike?

lessons.title: Does your town or city have a mall?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Kyle. I am from the UK. My question today is, does your town or city have a mall?

My town has a big mall. It has many shops for many things. It has clothes stores, shoe stores, department stores. It has a wide range of stores and restaurants. My favorite store is the shoe store because I like to buy shoes.
Does your town or city have a mall?

lessons.title: Is Jazz music interesting for you?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Lyra. I am from Kosovo. My question is, is jazz music interesting?

Yes. Jazz music is very interesting. I like this type of music. I sometimes listen to it. Jazz music is not popular in my country. This music is popular in America. Jazz music sounds very unique. A lot of people love jazz music.
What do you think? Is jazz music interesting?
Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. My question is, is your shirt comfortable?

Yes. This black shirt is comfortable. This shirt is very soft. I like this shirt, but is this orange shirt comfortable? No. This shirt is not comfortable. This shirt is not soft. This shirt is scratchy.
My question for you is, is your shirt comfortable?
Hello, my name is Susan. I am from Armenia. My question is, where is your house?

My house is in Armenia. I live in a village. My village is not small. It is in the mountains. There are a lot of trees and flowers. The nature there is wonderful. There are forests around us. There are many mountains in front of our house. There is a church at the top of one of the mountains. I like it a lot. The view is amazing.
Tell me about your house. Where is it?

lessons.title: Who do you meet every day?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from America, and my question is, who do you meet every day?

I meet my friend every day. Her name is Megan. She is tall. She has brown hair. I drive to a coffee shop every morning. I see her there. Megan works at the coffee shop. I order tea. I sometimes order a sweet snack. I talk with Megan about work. I do not talk about problems. She talks to me about events at the coffee shop. I do not meet my other friend, Madison, every day. She works at a hospital. I meet her on Saturday and Sunday.
My question for you is who do you meet every day?
Hi, my name is Maggie. I am from America, and my question is, where are you from?

I am from Springfield. Springfield is a city in America. There are 67 cities in America named Springfield. I am from the Springfield that is in Missouri. Missouri is a state in the middle of America. I like Springfield.

My Springfield is not big, but there are many things to do. There are many restaurants, parks, and shops. There are not any beaches in Springfield, and there are not any mountains, but there are many rivers and lakes.
Where are you from?
Hello, my name is Kyle. I am from the UK and my question for you today is, what desserts do you like? What desserts do you like?
I like cheesecake. I like brownies. I like ice cream. I don't like mouse. I don't like tiramisu. I don't like custard.
What desserts do you like?
Hello. My name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, do you order food online?

Yes, I order food online. It is very simple and quick. I am sometimes lazy and tired. I usually get pizza or kebab. The food comes in 30 minutes. I also order groceries online. I get drinks, vegetables, and meat. The supermarket is far away from my house. I can save time. It is very convenient.
Do you buy groceries online?

lessons.title: Where do you go in the morning?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Lyra. I am from Kosovo. My question is, where do you go in the morning?

I don't go anywhere in the morning. I like to stay home. In the morning, I always sleep. I am not a morning person. I am a night person. I wake up very late. I love to stay home in the morning. I like my mornings peaceful and quiet.
What about you? Where do you go in the morning?

lessons.title: What shop sells clothes for teens?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Julie. I'm from America. Today's question is what shop sells clothes for teens?

My niece is 13 years old. She is a teenager. She shops at H&M. H&M is a shop. H&M sells clothes for teens. My niece buys shirts, shorts, pants, dresses, sweaters, socks, shoes, and many other things at H&M. She shops at H&M with her friends.
My question for you is what shop sells clothes for teens in your country?

lessons.title: Do you have a big yard?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Syuzan. I am from Armenia. My question is, do you have a big yard?

I live in a village. We have a big yard in front of our house. There are a lot of trees and flowers there. We grow vegetables and fruits. I don't take care of our yard. My grandfather takes care of it. We also have animals there. My grandfather keeps many pigs and chickens. We don't have a dog. I usually walk in our yard. I relax there. I read books there. I love it.
And you, do you have a big yard?

lessons.title: Do you have a zoo in your town?

lines.text: Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from America, and my question is, do you have a zoo in your town?

I do not have a zoo in my town. My town is small. It has many animals. It has raccoons, it has squirrels, it has dogs and cats, it has ducks, but it does not have a zoo. I visit the zoo in a another town. It is a nice zoo. It is a small zoo. It does not have elephants, but it has giraffes. It has big birds, it has zebras. It does not have tigers, it does not have lions. But I love to visit the zoo. I can feed the farm animals there.
My question for you is, do you have a zoo in your town?
Hello, my name is Miyu. I'm from Japan. My question is, where do you eat lunch?

I normally eat lunch at the cafeteria. The cafeteria is in the office. It is on the ground floor. The cafeteria has many options. I eat noodles a lot. I sometimes eat sandwiches. The cafeteria doesn't have pizza or hamburgers. The food is very cheap. My colleague does not eat in the cafeteria. She eats at her desk.
Where do you have lunch?
Hello, my name is Elizabeth. I am from America. And my question is, do you exercise in winter?

Yes, I exercise in winter. I like to walk my dog. I walk my dog to the park. I walk two hours a day. I do not belong to a gym. I like to exercise by myself. I lift weights at my house. I ride my bike. It is cold outside, but I like to exercise inside. I run outside. I run with my friend on the street. I run twice a week. I like to race, so I need to practice. Yes, I like to exercise in winter. It is not as hot as summer.
My question for you is, do you exercise in winter?
Hello, my name is Julie. I am from America. The question is, who is your friend?

My friend is Cecilia. Cecilia is my friend. Cecilia is 45 years old. I'm 45 years old. Cecilia is a mom. I am a mom. Ingrid and Astrid are Cecilia's daughters. Lila is my daughter. Cecilia is Argentine. She is from Argentina. I am from America. I am not from Argentina .
My question for you is, who is your friend?

lines.text: Yum!

lines.text: What snacks do you like?

lines.text: I like to eat fruit .

lines.text: Oh yeah? And what fruits do you like?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I like apples and oranges . And you?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I like strawberries and watermelon .

lines.text: Do you like to eat cookies ?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Of course! I love chocolate chip cookies .

lines.text: What do you do in the morning?

lines.text: I wake up . I take a shower. I get dressed, and I eat breakfast.

lines.text: Oh! When do you get up ?

lines.text: I fix and sell bikes.

lines.text: Sounds fun.

lines.text: What do you do at lunch?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, they need space for their kids.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: When is our meeting?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It is not until 2.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Are we in room 213?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, not anymore.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: OK, where is the meeting then?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Our new room is 216.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I like the new offfice. So, where is my desk?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yours is over there. It is next to mine .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Nice. And where is Jill's desk?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Hers is over there.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Where is Bob's desk?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: His is in the back, by the window.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What languages do you speak?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I speak English and I study Spanish .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That's cool. Do you have friends from Spain ?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, but I like Mexican TV shows.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Me too. I love movies in Spanish .

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah. Spanish is so cool!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you like Japanese food?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, I love Japanese food. I lived in Japan before.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, do you speak Japanese ?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Some. I have Japanese friends. I practice with them.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do they speak English ?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, they speak English very well.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What foods do you like?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I like French food and Thai food.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Me too. I also love Chinese food.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Do you like Korean food?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Yes, and I also love K-Pop.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: What is K-POP?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: K-POP is Korean pop music.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you like football?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, I love football. I watch German football, Italian football, Spanish football.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Me too, I want to go to England to watch my team.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: What is your team?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Chelsea. They play in the English Premiere League.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Oh! My favorite team in AC Milan. They play in Italy .

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: What sports can you play?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I can play baseball a bit and I can play tennis pretty well.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Can you play football?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, I'm terrible at football. What about you?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah. I can play football. I like it a lot, but I'm not great.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I bet you are pretty good .

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, really. I'm not that good .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What languages can you speak?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can speak Japanese and French.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Wow! Can you write in Japanese?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can write a little bit, but not that much.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Yeah. I hear Kanji is really difficult.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah. It's really difficult. What about you? What languages can you speak?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I can speak some Spanish, but not great. I can also speak Thai.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Wow! Can you write in Thai?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, but I can read it. Writing is really difficult.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Still, that's pretty cool!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: So, are you a good cook?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Not really. But I can cook basic stuff.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Yeah? What can you cook?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can make pasta dishes and some French cuisine. What about you?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I can't cook anything. I can only make an omelet.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: That's not too bad. Can you make pancakes?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, I can't even make that.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What are you doing tonight?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I am going to karaoke with friends. Do you want to come?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, thanks. I can't sing at all .

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Oh, you should come. Singing is fun!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Maybe for you. I hear you can sing really well.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I can sing a little bit, but I am not great .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That's not what I heard.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What do you do on the weekend?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I usually stay home, but sometimes I go out.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, where do you go?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Sometimes I go to the beach. Sometimes, I go to the park.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I often go there, too. Do you ever go to the lake?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, very rarely . It is too far from my house.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What do you usually have for dinner?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I try to eat healthy, so I usually cook vegetables.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Really? What kind of stuff do you make?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Sometimes , I make soups. Sometimes , I make stir-fry.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Stir-fry! That”s not very healthy.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I know, but I don't eat it often .

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Do you take the bus to work?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, I never take the bus. I always drive.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah, it's so much easier to drive.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you drive to work?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Actually, I rarely drive. I usually walk to work. I live near the office.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Lucky you!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you ever go to the movies?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I rarely do. It is too expensive. Do you?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, not often . I usually rent DVDs.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Really? I never do that. I usually stream movies.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Nice. Do you have fast Internet?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah, usually it is fast, but sometimes it’s slow.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Excuse me, is there a gym in the hotel?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, there’s one on the first floor.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Great! And is there a pool?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, there’s a pool on the roof.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Is there a changing room up there?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, there isn’t , but there’s a restroom.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: OK, thanks.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: So, what is there to do in your town?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Well, there is a mall, a cinema, and there are a few parks.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, parks, nice. I love nature. Which one do you recommend?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I think Central City park is the best. There’s a huge garden there.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Is there parking nearby?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah, there’s a huge parking lot across the street.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What is there to eat?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Ah, there is some pasta in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Mm, I just had pasta for lunch. What else is there ?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Well, there is some stuff to make sandwiches.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That will do. Where is the bread?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: There’s some in the cupboard I think.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Are there any exchange students at your school?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, there are a few.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Really. What countries are they from?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Ah, let’s see. There is one student from Italy, and there are a few students from France.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, cool. Is there anyone from Paris?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, they are all from Leon!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How was the movie?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It was really good.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Was it scary?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, it was really scary.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Nice. Was it crowded?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, it wasn’t . There weren’t many people there, surprisingly.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Where were you last night?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I was at work.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Really? I was at your shop. You weren’t there.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, I was in the back working.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: You were ?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Really! I was there.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How was the test?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It was really hard.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How long was it?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: There were about 20 problems.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Yeah? What was your score?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Let’s just say, it wasn’t great, but it wasn’t bad either.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you know who was at the party?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Jason was there. So was Sue.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, were Tom and Katie there?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, they weren’t there, but their son was .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, I see. So, was it fun?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yeah, it was a fun evening.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What did you do yesterday?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Nothing much. I just stayed at home and cleaned the house. And you? What did you do?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: I drove to the mountains and went hiking.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: That sounds fun!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: It was . The weather was perfect, and we saw lots of animals.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Oh? What did you see?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: We saw some deer, an eagle, and a bear!

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Wow! How exciting! Did you take any pictures?

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Yes, I took a lot of photos. I'll post them online soon.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Please do!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Did you do anything this weekend?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I did . I took the train to the city and met my friend.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, yeah! What did you do?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: We had lunch and did some shopping.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Did you buy anything?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, I didn’t . I just went window shopping. I need to save money.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Me, too!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How was your day?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Difficult. I was so busy.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How so? What happened at work?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: A tour bus came in the restaurant for lunch. They ordered a lot of food. We only had two waiters, so we were very busy.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Did you get a big tip?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: We did . They left us $50!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Welcome home! What did you do tonight?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I went to the movies with my friends.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Fun! What did you see?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: We saw the new James Bond movie.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How was it? I heard it was good.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It was really good. I liked it a lot.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Did you do anything afterwards?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, we went to a cafe after the movie and talked a bit.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Did you eat? We ordered pizza.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, I had dinner at the cafe.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Well, if you're still hungry, there's still some pizza in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Thanks, but I'm full. I ate a big sandwich.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you have a pen? I forgot mine.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I don't have a pen, but I have a pencil.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That works. Do you have an eraser?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: The pencil has an eraser.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Perfect. And, do you have any paper?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: My gosh, you don’t have anything!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Would you like a sandwich?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I would love a sandwich.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: And some chips?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Some chips sound lovely.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How about a drink? Do you want a soda, or some iced tea?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I’m OK. I have a water.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you want the water in a glass with ice?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, the bottle is fine.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How do you like your new house?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It’s nice. It has a kitchen, a big bedroom, and a nice bathroom.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What is the kitchen like?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It is big, and it has a big stove.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What about the bathroom?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: It does not have a bathtub, but it has a shower.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you have a yard?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, but the yard is small. It does have a nice tree though.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Nice! Do you have a nice view?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, the view is terrible. There is a tall building next door.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How was the wedding party? Did you have fun?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, it was fun. The food was delicious.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: What food did they have?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: There was a salad bar, a drink bar, and a buffet.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That sounds nice! Was there a band?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, but there was a DJ.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Cool! How was the music?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Not great. All the songs they played were really old.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That sounds like a boring party.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, it was fun. The atmosphere was good. Everyone had a good time.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do you have any paper?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I have some , but not much.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: How much do you have?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I have about 10 sheets of paper.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, that is plenty. I just need five sheets.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: OK, here you go.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Do we have any eggs?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: We have some. Maybe three eggs.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: OK, and do we have any cheese?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, we don’t have any cheese.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, that’s too bad. I want to make an omelet.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Well, I can go to the store and buy some .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: No, that’s OK. I’ll just have toast.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Care for some coffee?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I would love some .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Cream or sugar?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No sugar, but I’ll take a little cream, please!

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh, you know what, we don’t have any cream. Is milk OK?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: That’s fine.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: So, what did you get for lunch?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I bought some stuff to make sandwiches.

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: Oh great! Did you buy any potato chips?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: No, I did not. I did not see any .

lines.speaker: Man
lines.text: That’s OK. We have some pretzels.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: That will work.
